key_insight: In de novo Parkinson's disease, cognitive decline appears driven by accelerated neurodegeneration on top of pre-existing white matter hyperintensity burden, rather than by faster WMH accumulation itself.
clinical_relevance: Baseline vascular brain injury and a decline-related atrophy pattern may help identify patients at higher risk for multidomain progression, including cognition, gait, function, and neuropsychiatric symptoms.
method: Longitudinal PPMI cohort of newly diagnosed, untreated PD participants who were cognitively normal at baseline.
Linear mixed-effects models tracked atrophy, WMH burden, and clinical trajectories over at least 3 years.
Mixed-effects analyses tested how baseline WMH and baseline atrophy-pattern expression related to later multidomain progression.
evidence_signal: The study compared 58 cognitive decliners with 292 stable participants and found significant converter-dependent associations across multiple outcomes, with q-values below 0.05 and the strongest interaction for MoCA (q<0.001).
watch_item: These findings are observational and from a selected cohort, so they support risk stratification rather than proving causation or direct treatment benefit.
paper_title: Vascular and neurodegenerative contributions to cognitive decline and multidomain progression in de novo Parkinsons disease
